clue.text: Sporting sides gathering for each broadcast

indicators.note: the jumbled sides gathers another piece into its middle, holding it inside
sporting in the sense of frolicking or playing about tells us the word sides is rearranged

parts.note: per is Latin for each, as in per head

explanation.surface: Team sides assembling for a television or radio broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sporting' looks like it describes the sides as athletic teams; it really signals a rearrangement, with 'gathering' doing the enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: To broadcast seed is to scatter it widely, the same sense as spreading things out over an area.

clue.text: In school I'm surprised to feel too hot

indicators.note: one piece sits in the other, so the exclamation goes inside the abbreviation for school

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'gosh'

explanation.surface: A pupil is startled to find the classroom overheated.
explanation.walkthrough: Cor is everyday British slang for surprise, as in 'Cor blimey!'. 'to' is a link word before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorching weather is weather so hot it burns, so to scorch is to be or feel excessively hot.

clue.text: Top apartment, dry, secured by retiring spies

indicators.note: secured by means held inside, so one piece is enclosed by the other
retiring means going backwards, so the letters for the spies are read in reverse

parts.note: the CIA is the American intelligence agency, a body of spies
TT, teetotal, means abstaining from alcohol, that is dry

explanation.surface: A rooftop flat with no alcohol, kept safe by spies who are stepping back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' looks like shy, and 'dry' like the weather; dry here is teetotal, a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: An attic is the room at the very top of a house, under the roof.

clue.text: Island maidens go along, skirting current fire

parts.note: I is a standard abbreviation for island on maps
M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over

indicators.note: skirting means going round the edge of, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: to pass on is to go along, move further
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Women on an island walk past an electric current that sets things alight.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored. 'fire' is a verb here: to inflame.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire someone up is to fill them with passion, the meaning of this rare verb.

clue.text: Listen, hearing creditor approaching?

indicators.note: hearing tells us the phrase is taken by its sound, as heard

parts.note: a creditor is a lender, and approaching means near, so this is a lender who is near

explanation.surface: Pay attention: you can hear the moneylender coming.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'lender near' sounds like the three-word phrase that means listen.
explanation.definitionFit: To lend an ear is an idiom for paying attention, giving someone your hearing.

clue.text: Presume sick friend hasn't died

indicators.note: sick here means unwell, out of order, so the letters are rearranged
hasn't means lacks, so one letter is removed from the word friend

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: Someone guesses that an ill friend has not passed away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hasn't' drops D from FRIEND to leave FRIEN, and 'sick' rearranges those five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To infer is to conclude from evidence, to suppose that something is so.

clue.text: Last of stops moved forward on city transport

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another comes after it

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London

indicators.note: last of points to the final letter of the word for stops as the one that shifts
moved forward means that final letter is shifted earlier in the word

parts.note: stays means stops, as in stays put

explanation.surface: The final stop is brought forward on the city's bus route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'city transport' wants to be buses; 'transport' alone is the definition, meaning rapture, and 'on' places the moved-forward word after the City postcode.
explanation.definitionFit: A transport of delight is a state of overwhelming joy or rapture.

clue.text: Where you could find Jack having row with daughter?

definitions.text: Where you could find Jack having row with daughter?

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, and AB, able seaman, is a sailor too
an oar is what you row with

explanation.surface: A sailor and his daughter rowing out to a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack (Jack tar) is a sailor, AB. The whole clue also says where a sailor rowing with his daughter is found: on the ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor is found on board a ship, that is on the vessel.

clue.text: Nobody welcomes new peer

indicators.note: welcomes means takes in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a squit is British slang for an insignificant person, a nobody

explanation.surface: An unimportant person greets a new member of the House of Lords.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peer' looks like a lord but is the verb. SQUIT is British slang for a worthless little person; 'welcomes' puts N inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To peer is to look narrowly with half-closed eyes, which is what this verb means.

clue.text: By grabbing right jug you could find something to drink here

definitions.text: you could find something to drink here

indicators.note: grabbing means holding inside, so the word by holds the other pieces

parts.note: an ewer is a large water jug

explanation.surface: Grab the right jug and you'll find a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grabbing' puts R and EWER inside the letters B and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A brewery makes beer, so it is a place where drink is found.

clue.text: Coaches regularly taken by an Indian perhaps

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter, here the second, fourth and sixth of coaches

explanation.surface: Coaches often carry a passenger from India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indian' looks like a person but is the Indian Ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian is one example of an ocean, along with the Atlantic and Pacific.

clue.text: Articulate aunt and niece exchanging letters

indicators.note: exchanging letters means the letters of the two words swap about, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A well-spoken aunt and her niece are writing to each other.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures letters in the post; really the letters of AUNT and NIECE are shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: To articulate is to pronounce words clearly, the verb meaning to speak distinctly.

clue.text: Where to expect fourth queue for "Spellbound"?

parts.note: a queue is expected at the way in of a building, so this is the place a queue is found
queues lettered A, B, C, D make the fourth one queue D

explanation.surface: Where would a fourth line form for a film called Spellbound?
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one picture: the doorway where queue D waits, as at a cinema with lettered queues.
explanation.definitionFit: Spellbound and entranced both mean held as if by magic, fascinated.

clue.text: Inspire Tory's proclamation, having taken line out

indicators.note: having taken goes with out: the letter for line is taken from the phrase
out completes the instruction to remove a letter from the proclamation

parts.note: a Tory, whose party colour is blue, might proclaim 'I'm blue'

explanation.surface: A Conservative's announcement fires people up once a line is cut.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue is the colour of Britain's Conservative (Tory) party; take L out of I'M BLUE.
explanation.definitionFit: To imbue is to fill or inspire someone with a feeling or quality.

clue.text: Ancient wig from Britain imported by old man in Paris

indicators.note: imported by means brought inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: pere is French for father, an old man in slang
UK, United Kingdom, stands for Britain

explanation.surface: An old wig from Britain bought by a Parisian father.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old man' is slang for father; in Paris that becomes the French word. 'Ancient' marks the wig as long out of fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: A peruke was a periwig, the long powdered hairpiece of the 17th and 18th centuries.

clue.text: Not so much returned in sweep, as hospital's lost capital

indicators.note: in places the reversed piece inside the other
lost means a letter is removed, here the one for hospital

parts.note: to brush is to sweep
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

indicators.note: returned means turned back, so the word for not so much reads backwards

parts.note: less means not so much

explanation.surface: Sweeping less than before, as the hospital has lost its principal city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not so much returned' reads as a reduced sweep; the reversal gives SSEL, and the brush minus hospital gives BRUS for it to sit in. 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This city is the capital of Belgium and seat of the EU.

clue.text: Perfect pilot, not female but more like the female, it's said

definitions.text: more like the female, it's said

parts.note: dead can mean exact or perfect, as in dead centre

indicators.note: not means the letter for female is missing from the word for pilot

parts.note: a flier is a pilot

explanation.surface: A flawless pilot, male not female, though said to be more dangerous like a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Kipling's line says 'the female of the species is more deadly than the male', hence 'it's said'.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverbial saying holds that females are more lethal, so more like them means more lethal.

clue.text: Attack observations that have been written up

indicators.note: in a down clue, written up means read from bottom to top, so the letters go backwards

parts.note: notes are observations, remarks

explanation.surface: A critique of comments that have since been published.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written up' looks like 'published'; in a down clue it reverses NOTES.
explanation.definitionFit: To set on someone is to attack them, as a dog is set on a burglar.

clue.text: Dodgy reclaim OK with taxman!

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or crooked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A taxman approving a dubious claim with an exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link. The definition is the punctuation mark that ends the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The printed symbol at the end of the clue is the one called by this name.

clue.text: Experiencing power cut, Queen Mary maybe awfully cold

indicators.note: experiencing goes with cut: the ship suffers a loss of the letter for power
cut means removed, so the letter for power is dropped

parts.note: the Queen Mary is an ocean liner, an example of a ship
P is the physics abbreviation for power
awfully means very, as in awfully nice

explanation.surface: A liner suffering a power failure is very cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen Mary' suggests royalty, but it is the liner. 'Experiencing ... cut' takes P out of SHIP, leaving SHI.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling shivery means trembling with cold, chilled.

clue.text: What fumbling server in fish bar might give to buy it?

definitions.text: What fumbling server in fish bar might give
definitions.meaning: a clumsy worker at a fish-and-chip shop could drop the customer's change into the food
to buy it is slang for to die

explanation.surface: A clumsy chip-shop server's mistake with the money.
explanation.walkthrough: A fish bar is a British fish-and-chip shop. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to die, from gamblers cashing in their counters at the end of play.

clue.text: Back up troops forming part of the squad?

parts.note: RE are the Royal Engineers, British army troops
forming part of means in, contained in
a force is a body of people such as a squad

explanation.surface: Is it the backup troops who make up the team?
explanation.walkthrough: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a British army corps; read as Engineers in the force.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinforce is to strengthen or support, to back something up.

clue.text: Infertile area ignored by republic

indicators.note: ignored by means left out, so the letter for area is dropped from the country

parts.note: Hungary is a republic in central Europe

explanation.surface: A barren region the republic has overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as geography; the area is the letter A dropped from HUNGARY.
explanation.definitionFit: Hungry land is poor, barren soil, an old sense of the word.

clue.text: Ancient city: leave, having gone into it

indicators.note: having gone into means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: it means sex appeal, abbreviated SA
to part is to leave, go away

explanation.surface: Quit an old Greek city after entering it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' as sex appeal (SA) is a crossword convention; PART goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparta was a city-state of classical Greece, famed for its warriors.

clue.text: Appropriate Home Counties man on a mission?

parts.note: the Home Counties around London are in the south-east of England, SE
a quester is one who goes on a quest, a mission

explanation.surface: A suitable man from the commuter belt is on a mission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' looks like an adjective but is the verb: to take possession. The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London.
explanation.definitionFit: To sequester property is to seize or appropriate it.

clue.text: Fire visible from below in mountains

parts.note: a pyre is a heap of wood set on fire, a bonfire

indicators.note: in a down clue, from below means read upwards, so the letters go backwards

parts.note: seen means visible

explanation.surface: A fire can be seen from the valley in the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from below' reverses SEEN to make NEES.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pyrenees are the mountain range between France and Spain.

clue.text: Ditch Yank, wanting time for wife

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so one letter goes missing
time for wife says one letter replaces the other

parts.note: to yank is to pull hard, to wrench

explanation.surface: An American dumps his wife, needing time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yank' looks like an American but is the verb, to pull: WRENCH with T replacing W.
explanation.definitionFit: A trench is a long narrow ditch dug in the ground.

clue.text: Slip black article out of wash

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: out of means taken out, so the article is removed

parts.note: to launder is to wash clothes
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A dark garment slips out of the laundry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' drops A from LAUNDER, leaving LUNDER.
explanation.definitionFit: A blunder is a careless mistake, a slip.

clue.text: Happen to see me intercepting great stroke

indicators.note: intercepting means getting in the way of, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a coup is a great stroke, a brilliant success

explanation.surface: By chance you see me interrupting a masterstroke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to see' is a link: the definition is 'Happen'.
explanation.definitionFit: When something comes up, it occurs or arises unexpectedly.

clue.text: Make slow progress — better when stripped

indicators.note: stripped means the outer layers are removed, both end letters

parts.note: a better is one who bets, a gambler

explanation.surface: Slowing down improves things when you lose layers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' is not 'improved' but one who bets; strip its ends.
explanation.definitionFit: To amble is to walk at a slow, relaxed pace.
